name: Oberau
kurzbeschreibung: The main town of Wildschönau, featuring the baroque parish church, a top ski area, and traditional customs.
beschreibung:
Overview

Oberau is situated on a sun-drenched plateau in the heart of the 24-kilometer-long alpine highland valley of the Wildschönau within the Kitzbühel Alps, in the Kufstein district of Tyrol, roughly 14 kilometers south of Wörgl at an altitude of 936 meters. Serving as the geographical and administrative capital of the four-village municipality of Wildschönau (comprising Niederau, Oberau, Auffach, and Thierbach), the village hosts the municipal hall, local schools, and a vibrant community life. With around 2,100 residents in the parish area, Oberau forms the lively core of the valley. The village landscape is characterized by imposing Tyrolean farmhouses, flower-laden wooden balconies, and lush alpine meadows framed by the peaks of the Schatzberg and Rosskopf. Oberau blends authentic rural traditions with modern family leisure facilities, serving as a versatile gateway for hiking and winter sports.

History

Settlement in the Wildschönau began in the 12th century through systematic forest clearing overseen by the Bishops of Salzburg and Regensburg. A church in Oberau was first officially recorded in 1394 regarding an endowed mass. In 1719, a catastrophic fire laid waste to the medieval church and much of the village center. Between 1751 and 1752, the present monumental Baroque parish church of St. Margaret was erected according to plans by master builder Johann Holzmeister from the Zillertal; acclaimed as the 'Cathedral of the Wildschönau', it impresses with its 52-meter onion-domed steeple and magnificent Rococo frescoes by Christoph Anton Mayr. The valley also earned historical fame through an exclusive imperial decree granted by Empress Maria Theresa, endowing local farmers with the unique monopoly to distill 'Krautinger', a pungent schnapps made from white turnips, a protected regional specialty to this day.

Getting There

Reaching Oberau is straightforward thanks to its proximity to the lower Inn Valley corridor. By car, drivers leave the A12 Inntal Autobahn at exit Wörgl Ost and ascend the well-maintained L3 Wildschönauer Landesstraße through Niederau straight to Oberau (about 14 kilometers, taking around 15 minutes from the motorway). Rail travelers use the international junction of Wörgl Hauptbahnhof, where Austrian Railjets and German ICE trains stop regularly. From Wörgl station square, frequent VVT regional buses (route 4064) operate hourly directly into Oberau village center. Overnight visitors holding the Wildschönau Card enjoy complimentary bus and ski shuttle travel throughout the valley.

Tips

A flagship attraction for families is the Drachental Wildschönau leisure park right in the village, anchored by the 'Drachenflitzer' alpine coaster—a thrilling two-kilometer rail toboggan track featuring three giant 25-meter loops—accompanied by an adventure lake and climbing grounds. In the hamlet of Bach, the Mountain Farming Museum z'Bach inside an authentic 1795 timber farmstead offers a fascinating journey into rural heritage; every Thursday, local craftsmen demonstrate traditional trades like turning and spinning at the craft market while serving fresh pastries. Walkers enjoy the scenic Franziskusweg trail to Niederau adorned with bronze sculptures by Hubert Flörl. In winter, the nearby Schatzberg connects into the Ski Juwel Alpbachtal Wildschönau ski area, while night tobogganing thrives at Roggenboden.
